title: Characters workflow
author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
selftext:
One thing which AI still seems to struggle to do is Characters. Yesterday i decided to test how far i can get GPT to create random weird characters animations.

My workflow is this.

Create image with an image AI (i used Qwen image pro) -> texture and rig it in meshy -> ask GPT to clean it up in blender -> ask GPT to animate it.

I was wondering if anyone has any better workflow for Characters animations.

Note: her movement is purposely weird. I asked GPT to move any limb it can. And this was done in 2 hours, if someone actually put efforts into it, it could look better for sure.

comments.author: AliAlHamwi
comments.body:
Four handoffs is where this hurts. Qwen makes the image, Meshy rigs it, GPT and Blender clean it, GPT animates it, and every hop quietly loses orientation, scale or skinning. The last tool inherits all the damage, which is why the movement reads possessed even before the deliberate weirdness. Collapsing the middle is the workflow upgrade: image to 3D with the rig and base animations in one place, then Blender only for the last mile. That collapse is what Ludo.ai's 3D generator does, auto rigging plus animation presets after image-to-3D, and I work on it, so take the shortcut suggestion with that in mind. Meshy's own rigging is the same idea if you would rather stay where you are.

The day and night thing you noticed is real, by the way. Low light hides surface noise. If she only looks right at night, the texture is telling you exactly where the cleanup pass has to go.
